name: Sun
description: The Sun is a G-type main-sequence star at the centre of the Solar System. It holds 99.86% of the system's mass and dictates the orbits of every planet, moon, and small body.

name: Mercury
description: Mercury is the smallest planet and the closest to the Sun. It is a heavily cratered and airless world in 3:2 spin-orbit resonance with the Sun.

name: Venus
description: Venus is a rocky planet wrapped in a thick carbon-dioxide atmosphere. Surface temperatures are high enough to melt lead, hotter than Mercury due to the greenhouse effect.

name: Earth
description: Earth is the only known world with liquid-water oceans and life. Its axial tilt and 24-hour rotation give rise to seasons and a protective magnetic field.

name: Moon

labels.name: Sea of Tranquility
labels.fact: Site of the first crewed landing by NASA astronauts Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin on 20 July 1969.
labels.imageAlt: Apollo 11 landing site at the Sea of Tranquility

labels.name: Tycho Crater
labels.fact: 108 million year old crater with a diameter of 85km discovered by Tycho Brahe.

description: Earth's only natural satellite, tidally locked so the same face always points home. Its dry, cratered surface still carries the marks of Apollo landings.

name: Mars

labels.name: Olympus Mons
labels.fact: Largest volcano and tallest known planetary mountain in the Solar System, rising about 22 km above the surrounding plains. It is a vast shield volcano formed by repeated eruptions of low-viscosity basaltic lava.

labels.name: Tharsis Montes
labels.fact: Three enormous shield volcanoes (Ascraeus Mons, Pavonis Mons, and Arsia Mons) aligned along the Tharsis region of Mars.

labels.name: Valles Marineris
labels.fact: Gigantic canyon system stretching roughly 4,000 km across the surface, several times longer and deeper than the Grand Canyon.

labels.name: Perseverance
labels.fact: NASA rover that landed in Jezero Crater in 2021 to search for signs of ancient microbial life and study Mars's geological history. Collects and caches rock samples for future collection missions.
labels.imageAlt: Perseverance rover on the surface of Mars

labels.name: Curiosity
labels.fact: NASA rover exploring Gale Crater since landing in 2012. It studies Martian rocks, soil, atmosphere, and climate using a suite of scientific instruments.
labels.imageAlt: Curiosity rover on the surface of Mars

description: Mars is a cold desert planet with the tallest volcano and the longest canyon in the Solar System. Polar ice and ancient riverbeds hint at a wetter past.

name: Jupiter

labels.name: Great Red Spot
labels.fact: Persistent anticyclonic storm that produces wind speeds up to 496 km/h. It was first observed in 1831.

description: Jupiter is the largest planet, a hydrogen-helium giant with a faint ring system. Four large Galilean moons orbit nearby, with 100+ smaller moons in its orbit.

name: Saturn

labels.name: Saturn's Hexagon
labels.fact: Persistent hexagonal cloud pattern around the north pole, wider than two Earths.
labels.imageAlt: Saturn's north-polar hexagon, a teal six-sided storm with a dark central vortex

description: Saturn is a gas giant known for its broad, icy ring system. Its pale yellow hue is due to ammonia crystals in the upper atmosphere.

name: Uranus
description: Uranus is an ice giant that rolls on its side, with an axial tilt of about 82°. Methane in the atmosphere gives the planet its pale cyan colour.

name: Neptune

labels.name: Great Dark Spot
labels.fact: Intermittent anticyclonic storms with a shorter lifetime than Jupiter's spots.

description: Neptune is the most distant planet, an ice giant with the strongest winds in the Solar System. The Great Dark Spot seen by Voyager 2 has since faded and reformed.

name: Ganymede
description: Ganymede is the largest moon in the Solar System, bigger than Mercury. An iron core and a likely subsurface ocean make it the only moon with its own magnetic field.

name: Titan
description: Titan is Saturn's largest moon and the only satellite with a dense atmosphere. Lakes and rivers of liquid methane run across a water-ice crust.

name: Callisto
description: Callisto is the outermost Galilean moon, a heavily cratered ice-rock body. It is the most geologically quiet of Jupiter's large moons.

name: Io
description: Io is the most volcanically active body in the Solar System. Jupiter's tides flex its interior, feeding hundreds of sulfur volcanoes.

name: Europa
description: Europa is an ice-covered moon with a young, fractured crust. A global ocean of liquid water is thought to lie beneath, making it a prime target in the search for life.

name: Triton
description: Triton is Neptune's largest moon and orbits backwards relative to Neptune's spin. Nitrogen geysers and a captured, Pluto-like composition suggest it was once a Kuiper Belt object.
